issues.title: Latent inconsistency: functions.py:286-287 still references array_distinct for the `distinct` name (dead path today, footgun tomorrow)
issues.spec_citation: CQL §22 List Operators / Appendix B — distinct must preserve first-occurrence ordering and retain a single NULL element (same spec anchor as QA-001).
issues.evidence: In `fhir4ds/cql/translator/functions.py:286-287`, `_translate_list_func(name="distinct", ...)` returns `SQLFunctionCall(name="array_distinct", args=[source])` — the same DuckDB native call that caused QA-001. The engineer's scope-discipline note (engineer_handoff.md) correctly identifies this path is overridden upstream by the dedicated `DistinctExpression` AST node handler (`_translate_distinct_expression` in `_lists.py:897`), so it is NOT load-bearing for the spec-defined function form today. Verified by grep: every reference to `DistinctExpression` in the translator uses `_translate_distinct_expression`, and `_translate_list_func` is only reached via generic function-call fallback when no dedicated AST node exists. The risk is that a future code path that routes a `distinct(...)` call through the generic function dispatcher (e.g. via a partial migration, a new helper, or a parser edge case that bypasses the DistinctExpression AST node) would silently re-introduce the same NULL-dropping / order-violating behavior that QA-001 just fixed.
issues.impact: No live bug. Future regression risk only. Severity LOW because the dispatch path is unreachable today and the engineer documented it.
issues.recommended_fix: Either (a) delete the dead branch entirely with an assertion that `distinct` is always handled by `_translate_distinct_expression`, or (b) route it to `SQLFunctionCall(name='"Distinct"', args=[source])` for defense-in-depth parity with the fluent form. Option (b) is preferred — it makes the two paths self-consistent regardless of which dispatcher reaches them.

issues.title: Regression test TestFluentDistinctMacroEmission verifies SQL emission only, not runtime NULL retention or first-occurrence ordering
issues.spec_citation: CQL §22 / Appendix B — distinct must preserve first-occurrence ordering AND retain a single NULL element.
issues.evidence: `fhir4ds/cql/tests/unit/test_sql_structure.py::TestFluentDistinctMacroEmission` (lines 153–201) translates CQL to SQL and asserts the substring `"DISTINCT"(` appears and `ARRAY_DISTINCT` does not. It does NOT execute the SQL against DuckDB, so it cannot detect (a) NULL retention or (b) first-occurrence ordering. The macro `CQLListDistinctEq` was independently audited at the architect phase and DOES implement both invariants correctly via `generate_subscripts` + `NOT EXISTS previous equal element` filtering. However, if the macro definition were ever regressed (e.g. someone changed `CQLListDistinctEq` to call `array_distinct` internally), these tests would still pass while the runtime behavior silently breaks — the exact failure mode that allowed QA-001 to ship in the first place.
issues.impact: No live bug. The macro is correct today. Test-coverage gap only. Severity LOW because the existing macro-level tests in `fhir4ds/cql/duckdb/tests/` (referenced in AGENTS.md line 3679) cover `CQLListDistinctEq` directly, but those tests do not specifically cover the fluent-form dispatch path.
issues.fix_location: fhir4ds/cql/tests/unit/test_sql_structure.py (extend) or a new integration test that actually executes the emitted SQL.
issues.recommended_fix: Add a runtime test that registers the CQL macros, executes `"Distinct"([1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3])`, `"Distinct"([NULL, NULL, NULL])`, and `"Distinct"(['a', NULL, 'a'])` via DuckDB, and asserts `[1, 2, 3]`, `[None]`, and `['a', None]` respectively. This converts the regression test from emission-shaped to behavior-shaped, matching the SKEPTIC QA personality's key-question coverage.

issues.title: repeat inside enclosing forEachOrNull shares the same parent-row-drop leak shape that QA-005 just fixed for nested forEach
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 ViewDefinition, Process(S, N) step 3 (same anchor as QA-005). When the outer forEachOrNull foci is empty, ALL columns under that select — including those produced by a nested `repeat` — must bind to NULL and exactly one row must be emitted.
issues.evidence: In `fhir4ds/viewdef/generator.py:1546-1558`, the `repeat` branch in `_process_selects` calls `generate_repeat_unnest(resolved_paths, current_var, alias)` (from `fhir4ds/viewdef/unnest.py:112-136`) and emits a plain `CROSS JOIN LATERAL` with no `null_preserve_var` parameter. `generate_repeat_unnest` does not even accept a `null_preserve_var` parameter. When a `repeat` is nested under an enclosing `forEachOrNull` whose foci is empty, the OUTER LEFT JOIN preserves the parent NULL row, but the repeat's `CROSS JOIN LATERAL` evaluates `fhirpath_repeat(NULL_alias, paths)` -> empty collection -> CROSS JOIN against zero rows -> parent's preserved NULL row eliminated. This is the exact same bug shape as QA-005 for `forEach`. The QA-005 fix did not extend to `repeat` because QA-005's reproducer only exercised `forEach` (not `repeat`), and the engineer's scope discipline stayed within that reproducer.
issues.impact: Silent data loss for any ViewDefinition that uses `forEachOrNull: optionalField` wrapping `repeat: optionalField.deepPaths` — the parent resource disappears from the output when the optional outer field is absent. No live test covers this combination today. Severity MEDIUM (vs QA-005's HIGH) because `repeat` under `forEachOrNull` is a rarer authoring pattern than `forEach` under `forEachOrNull`, and no production or conformance ViewDefinition is known to use it. Filed as a NEW finding for a future iteration; not addressed in iter-3.
issues.recommended_fix: Mirror the QA-005 fix: (1) add a `null_preserve_var` parameter to `generate_repeat_unnest` that, when set, gates the VALUES row on `{null_preserve_var} IS NOT NULL` and UNION ALLs a single synthetic NULL row when `{null_preserve_var} IS NULL`. (2) Thread the already-plumbed `null_preserve_var` from `_process_selects` into the `generate_repeat_unnest` call. (3) Extend `_collect_foreachornull_paths` tracking if `repeat` is also a wrapper that should suppress null rows across UNION ALL alternatives (likely yes for symmetry). Add a regression test analogous to `TestForeachOrNullNestedForeachSpecSofVd05Historian` but with `repeat` instead of `forEach`.
issues.root_cause: `generate_repeat_unnest` emitted an unconditional CROSS JOIN LATERAL against `fhirpath_repeat(resource_var, paths)`. When `resource_var` was the unnest alias of an enclosing forEachOrNull whose foci was empty (preserved NULL row), `fhirpath_repeat(NULL_alias, paths)` returned an empty collection, the CROSS JOIN against zero rows eliminated the parent's preserved NULL row, and the entire selection structure collapsed to 0 rows — violating Process(S, N) step 3 (one null row total). Same bug shape as QA-005; the QA-005 fix only patched `generate_foreach_unnest`, leaving `generate_repeat_unnest` unfixed because QA-005's reproducer only exercised nested `forEach`.
issues.resolution: Mirrored QA-005 fix. (1) `fhir4ds/viewdef/unnest.py:generate_repeat_unnest` gained a `null_preserve_var` parameter; when set, the source VALUES row is gated on `{null_preserve_var} IS NOT NULL` and a synthetic NULL row is UNION ALLed only when `{null_preserve_var} IS NULL`. (2) `fhir4ds/viewdef/generator.py:_process_selects` repeat branch threads `null_preserve_var` into the call. (3) `_collect_foreachornull_paths` did NOT need extension: it tracks forEachOrNull *wrappers* (the dedup unit), not inner unnests; `repeat` (like nested `forEach`) is an inner unnest consumer of the null-preserving var, so the existing dedup correctly handles UNION ALL alternatives. Added regression tests in `TestForeachOrNullNestedRepeatSpecSofVd05Architect` (3 cases: outer-empty, outer-non-empty, mixed).

issues.title: AutoCoder.augment_resources lacks the isinstance(list) guard that QA-006 added to its sibling NotesPipeline.extract_conditions_batch — structural asymmetry
issues.spec_citation: API-contract consistency. The loader's two batch entry points (FHIRDataLoader.load_resources and NotesPipeline.extract_conditions_batch) both enforce isinstance(list) at entry; AutoCoder.augment_resources is the third batch entry point in the same package and does not.
issues.evidence: `fhir4ds/cql/loader/auto_coder.py:257-282` (`AutoCoder.augment_resources`) takes `resources: list[dict]` and only checks `if not resources: return` before iterating via `for resource in resources` at line 286. A string caller would char-iterate silently (each character passed to `augment_resource` which checks isinstance(dict) and logs a warning but does not raise); a dict caller would crash with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'slice'` only if `_augment_batch_parallel` is reached (which it is not, because workers default to 1); a generator caller would iterate once and exhaust. The QA-006 fix at notes_pipeline.py:391-394 added `isinstance(list)` to the sibling method but did not propagate to auto_coder.py. Realistic risk is LOW because `augment_resources` is only called from `fhir_loader.py:382`, which is downstream of `load_resources`'s isinstance guard at `:367` — the contract is enforced one layer up. The asymmetry is structural fragility, not a live bug.
issues.impact: No live bug today (the upstream caller enforces the contract). Future regression risk if a new caller invokes `augment_resources` directly without going through `load_resources`. Severity LOW because the existing call path is safe and the failure mode (silent string char-iteration) is the same shape QA-006 already characterized.
issues.fix_location: fhir4ds/cql/loader/auto_coder.py:281 (augment_resources entry, immediately after `if not resources: return`)
issues.recommended_fix: Add `if not isinstance(resources, list): raise TypeError(f'Expected list of FHIR resource dicts, got {type(resources).__name__}')` mirroring notes_pipeline.py:391-394. Two-line change with no behavioral impact on the existing call path.

issues.title: QA-017 pruning hardcodes CMS population-name strings (denominator_exclusion/numerator) in generic MeasureEvaluator logic; asymmetric vs denominator_exception
issues.spec_citation: GLOBAL_RULES 'Model Knowledge Must Be Data-Driven' — population names are FHIR R4 measure-population codes (http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/valueset-measure-population.html), but the causal-pruning relationship is a CMS eCQM Logic and Implementation Guidance rule, not a translator/evaluator branch. Acceptable to reference the canonical codes, but the asymmetric branch is fragile.
issues.evidence: `fhir4ds/dqm/evaluator.py:1541-1549` introduces a hardcoded branch keyed on `pop.audit_persona == AuditPersona.NUMERATOR and col_name == 'numerator' and 'denominator_exclusion' in df.columns`. The pruning only fires for the `denominator_exclusion -> numerator` causal pair. CMS eCQM logic has additional causal relationships that the same code shape should cover for narrative correctness: `denominator_exception -> numerator` (a patient in denominator_exception also has numerator unevaluated) and the reciprocal `denominator_exclusion -> numerator_exclusion` cases. The asymmetric implementation means narratives for the un-handled pairs will still show leaked evidence from the underlying audit SQL. Recommended fix: externalize the causal pairs to a small data-driven map (e.g., `_CAUSAL_SUPPRESSION_PAIRS: dict[str, set[str]] = {'numerator': {'denominator_exclusion', 'denominator_exception'}, ...}`) and iterate over it in `_prune`. No behavioral change for the existing `denominator_exclusion -> numerator` case; just generalizes the rule.

issues.title: _is_complex_function_arg docstring claims to exclude trivial comparison primitives but returns True for ALL SQLFunctionCall instances
issues.evidence: `fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_query.py:156-168`: `_is_complex_function_arg` docstring says 'Return True if `arg` is a SQLFunctionCall that is NOT a trivial comparison/equality primitive' but the body unconditionally `return True` for every SQLFunctionCall. The conservative behavior is intentional and correct (the QA-016 binder bug trigger is broad), but the docstring is misleading — a future maintainer reading the docstring may believe trivial comparisons are excluded and add a code path that relies on that. Recommended fix: either (a) update the docstring to say 'Returns True for any SQLFunctionCall — conservative because the binder trigger is broad' (preferred for honesty), or (b) actually exclude trivial comparison-shaped calls if benchmarking shows the narrow gate is safe.

issues.title: _fully_demote_audit_to_bool and _audit_chain_has_complex_leaf lack recursion-depth guards; rely on well-formed AST
issues.evidence: `fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_query.py:131-261`: Both helpers recurse through the SQL AST without depth tracking or a visited set. For well-formed ASTs produced by the translator this is fine, but: (1) `_fully_demote_audit_to_bool` recurses into `audit_leaf.args[0]` then through SQLFunctionCall args (line 197-220) — if a future translator bug emits a self-referential AST node, Python hits its recursion limit and the user gets an opaque RecursionError instead of a typed TranslationError. (2) `_audit_chain_has_complex_leaf` line 148-149 only traverses one level of SQLUnaryOp nesting; deeply-nested NOT NOT NOT EXISTS could be missed (returns False), causing the QA-016 binder bug to resurface. Recommended fix: add a `depth: int = 0` parameter with a sane limit (e.g., 64) that raises TranslationError on overflow, and either iterate or use an explicit stack for the unary-op descent.

issues.title: Closed-connection guard propagates the 'except duckdb.Error: pass' silent-swallow pattern to two new sites (core.py, fhir_loader.py)
issues.spec_citation: GLOBAL_RULES 'Error Hygiene' / 'No Silent Fallbacks'. Pre-existing pattern in cql/__init__.py:384-391; QA-015 propagates it.
issues.evidence: `fhir4ds/core.py:298-305` and `fhir4ds/cql/loader/fhir_loader.py:299-307` add a `con.execute('SELECT 1').fetchone()` probe with `except duckdb.Error: pass`. The intent is to distinguish `ConnectionException` (re-raised with a friendly message) from other DuckDB errors (swallowed because the connection is 'alive'). The risk: a real DuckDB internal error during the probe (e.g., a corrupted catalog) would be silently swallowed, then the subsequent real call would fail with a confusing error far from the probe. Acceptable as a defensive pattern (the probe is a no-op `SELECT 1`), but tracking it here so the pattern doesn't spread further. Recommended fix: narrow the swallow to `duckdb.InternalException` if such a type exists, or log a DEBUG line inside the swallow so a forensic query can find it.

issues.title: _suppress_null_preserved_row uses raw string replacement on generated SQL; depends on a single '\nWHERE ' marker appearing at the right scope
CMS2 SQL bloat from inline _latN.value disambiguation CASEs — replaced with SQL macros
issues.root_cause: _translate_is_type_check in fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_query.py:3244-3408 emitted inline 'CASE WHEN starts_with(LTRIM(R), '{') THEN json_extract_string(R, '$.start') IS NOT NULL ... ELSE FALSE END' blocks for CQL 'is Interval<DateTime>', 'is Interval<Quantity>', 'is Period', and 'is Range'. CMS2 referenced the same _latN.value 510+ times per CTE, producing ~150 KB of duplicated disambiguation CASE blocks (9.7% of the 1,552,792-byte noaudit SQL). A second inline CASE shape 'CASE WHEN starts_with(LTRIM(R), '{') THEN json_extract_string(R, '$.value') ELSE R END' for Quantity $.value extraction (fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_operators.py:6925-6941 and 7011-7027, and _functions.py:2008-2019) recurred 85 times (~600 KB). Prior attempts (Option A emission-time LATERAL hoisting, Option C post-translation AST dedup) failed because the audit emission path in cte_manager.py copies expression fragments verbatim into __pre_... CTEs, leaving dangling _disN/_latN alias references in scopes where those LATERAL joins are not visible.
issues.resolution: Option D: encapsulated the disambiguation logic in four globally-resolvable DuckDB SQL macros defined in fhir4ds/cql/duckdb/macros/clinical.py:50-89 (cql_value_is_period, cql_value_is_range, cql_value_is_interval_like, cql_quantity_value). Registered them via registerClinicalMacros, now wired into register_all_macros (fhir4ds/cql/duckdb/macros/__init__.py:67) so they are available in BOTH the native C++ extension path (extension.py:237) and the forced Python fallback path (core.py:241). Refactored the four inline CASE emission sites in fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_query.py:3254-3375 to emit SQLFunctionCall(name='cql_value_is_interval_like'/etc, args=[resource_expr]). Refactored the three Quantity $.value extraction sites in fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_operators.py:6925-6933 and 7009-7017, and fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_functions.py:2004-2012 to emit SQLFunctionCall(name='cql_quantity_value'). Unlike Option A/C, SQL macros are globally resolvable from any scope, so audit pre-compute CTEs that copy expression fragments verbatim can safely reference cql_value_is_period(x) without dangling.
